field_filtering_enforcement: STRUCTURAL, not honor-system: the specialist model can never disobey the allowlist because out-of-lane data never enters its context window. Mechanism — (1) Each agent file in .claude/agents/*.md carries machine-readable YAML frontmatter: `snapshot_fields:` and `trigger_fields:` lists of dot-paths into the REAL pydantic models (src/engine/snapshot.py Snapshot / src/engine/triggers.py Trigger), e.g. Atlas: [ref_price, clusters, target_menu, prior_day_high, prior_day_low, prior_week_high, prior_week_low, session_high, session_low, htf_regime, indicators.daily_vwap, indicators.daily_profile]; Helios: [ts, session, data_levels, indicators.ny_vwap]; Apollo: [ref_price, clusters, indicators.tfs, indicators.ny_vwap] + Trigger.[tf, direction, kind, pattern, htf_flag, wick_low, wick_high, cluster_center, confluence_count, close]; Hephaestus: [ref_price, target_menu, clusters] + Trigger.[entry_ref, stop_ref, wick_low, wick_high, direction, tf] (exact slices are the specialists' lane-owners' call; the runtime contract is that WHATEVER is declared is all they get). (2) The Desk runner (src/desk/runner.py, deterministic Python) implements `project(payload: dict, allowlist: list[str]) -> dict` — a pure function that walks dot-paths and builds a NEW dict containing only the declared subtree; the filtered dict is what gets serialized into the rendered prompt. The full Snapshot object is never passed to any prompt-rendering code path; the render function signature is render(agent_spec, filtered_snapshot, filtered_trigger) — there is no parameter through which the full Snapshot, account state, or another agent's verdict could even be threaded (independence enforced by call signature, per ai-workflow-rules 'specialists stay independent'). (3) Fail-closed path validation at STARTUP: every declared dot-path is resolved against Snapshot.model_json_schema() / Trigger.model_json_schema(); an unknown path (typo, or a Snapshot field renamed in a later engine change) aborts Desk startup — stale allowlists cannot silently ship empty slices. (4) Defense-in-depth deny assertion: before dispatch the runner asserts the serialized payload contains none of a hard-coded forbidden vocabulary (balance, pnl, prior_trade, trades_today, verdict) — these can't occur because Snapshot doesn't carry them (architecture.md Engine→Desk contract), but the assert catches future contract drift. (5) Hermes receives ONLY the four parsed specialist verdict JSONs plus trigger identity keys (ts, tf) — no Snapshot market fields at all (orchestration only, per the lane split). (6) The allowlist lives INSIDE the agent file, so changing an agent's visible fields changes the file's content hash → forces a version bump (see versioning) — an allowlist edit is a strategy change. Test coverage: test_desk_allowlist_filter renders real prompts from a fully-populated synthetic Snapshot and asserts out-of-lane field names AND values are absent from the exact prompt string.

failure_modes.mode: Invalid JSON from a specialist (unparseable, truncated, or fenced prose around JSON)
failure_modes.handling: Strict parse only (json.loads on the extracted tool/structured output; no lenient repair). Parse failure => that specialist's verdict = FAIL => unanimity broken => Hermes veto. Raw response bytes preserved as a content-addressed blob, journal row veto_reason=invalid_json with the blob ref. Per ai-workflow-rules this is ALSO a bug: the row is flagged agent_error=true so the nightly stats surface it for prompt-fix through the versioned-change gate.

failure_modes.mode: Schema violation (parses, but pydantic validation fails: missing gate, wrong enum, extra field, unanchored free-text where a bool is required)
failure_modes.handling: Each specialist's output schema is a pydantic model with extra='forbid' and every gate a strict bool keyed to its § reference. ValidationError => FAIL => veto, veto_reason=schema_violation, raw blob kept. No partial acceptance of 'mostly valid' output — a confidence score or prose where a pass/fail belongs is a schema violation by construction.

failure_modes.mode: Per-call timeout (specialist exceeds its 20 s budget)
failure_modes.handling: asyncio.wait_for cancels the call at the per-call timeout; specialist = FAIL => veto, veto_reason=timeout, latency_ms logged as the timeout value with timed_out=true. The other three specialists' completed verdicts are still journaled — partial evidence is audit data even when the trade is dead.

failure_modes.mode: Partial completion (e.g. 3 of 4 specialists return before the total deadline)
failure_modes.handling: Hermes assembly runs at min(all-returned, total-deadline). Any specialist without a valid parsed verdict at assembly time is a FAIL => veto, veto_reason=partial_completion listing the missing agent(s). Never wait past the deadline hoping for the straggler — the order window (§5, limit working promptly for the retest) is the binding constraint.

Exactly one retry, and only if elapsed wall-time leaves the retry inside the per-call budget (retry only when first failure occurred < 10 s in); otherwise immediate FAIL => veto, veto_reason=api_error with the SDK error class logged. retry_count recorded per agent per verdict. No exponential backoff loops — the 1m cadence forbids it; fail-closed and let the next trigger be graded fresh.

failure_modes.mode: Duplicate trigger (same candidate dispatched twice — restart, replayed queue, engine hiccup)
failure_modes.handling: Idempotency key = sha256 over the canonical Trigger fields (ts, tf, direction, kind) + snapshot content hash. Runner keeps a per-session-day dedupe set (rebuilt from the journal on restart); a duplicate is NOT re-graded — it writes a journal row outcome=duplicate_suppressed referencing the original verdict_id. Prevents double journal rows and double proposals reaching the Vault.

Two checks, both fail-closed: (a) IDENTITY: Snapshot.ts must exactly equal Trigger.ts (same closed candle — the Engine→Desk contract is one snapshot per trigger candle close); mismatch => veto, veto_reason=snapshot_trigger_ts_mismatch. (b) FRESHNESS: wall-clock at dispatch minus Trigger.ts > desk.staleness_limit_s (proposed 10 s; config/strategy.yaml desk block, CALIBRATE) => veto, veto_reason=stale_snapshot with the measured drift_ms logged. A verdict on a candle the market has already left cannot produce a §5-compliant working limit.

triggers._mtf_arbitrate keys by close ts and returns at most one Trigger per ts (§1 highest-TF-wins), so two triggers sharing a ts at the Desk boundary is an ENGINE INVARIANT VIOLATION: veto BOTH, veto_reason=engine_invariant_violation, and raise an operator alert (this is exactly the engine-bug class the Desk cross-check exists to catch). Distinct-ts triggers arriving while a prior grading is in flight are queued and graded strictly serially in ts order (the Desk is stateless per grading; §5.6 one-position-at-a-time is the Vault's job, and the Desk must NOT know about open positions — that would leak prior-trade state).

failure_modes.mode: Snapshot fails pydantic validation at the Desk boundary
failure_modes.handling: Snapshot.model_validate on ingest; failure => veto, veto_reason=invalid_snapshot, raw payload blob kept. The Desk never grades an object it cannot prove matches the contract.

failure_modes.mode: Agent-file hash mismatch at startup or dispatch (prompt edited without version bump)
failure_modes.handling: Runner refuses to start (or, if detected mid-session via mtime change, halts grading) — every candidate from that moment is vetoed with veto_reason=version_mismatch until the lockfile is reconciled. An unversioned prompt edit is an unversioned strategy change (ai-workflow-rules) and must be structurally impossible to run.

Write-ahead intent: before dispatching any model call, append an intent row (verdict_id, trigger identity, snapshot ref, dispatch ts). On restart, any intent row without a matching verdict row is closed out with a synthetic veto row, veto_reason=runner_crash. No grading ever vanishes from the audit trail.

failure_modes.mode: Journal write failure (disk full, schema-invalid row)
failure_modes.handling: Logging is on the critical path by design: if the journal row cannot be validated (JournalRow, extra='forbid') and appended, the Desk HALTS — no verdict may reach the Vault unlogged. §10 says every verdict is logged; an unloggable Desk is a stopped Desk.

determinism: Two-tier claim, stated honestly. TIER 1 — input determinism (guaranteed): the rendered request for a given (snapshot, trigger, agent version) is byte-identical across runs. Prompts contain NO wall-clock time, NO uuids/request-ids, NO account or environment state — only Snapshot.ts and the filtered slices; JSON serialization is canonical (sorted keys, fixed float formatting matching the engine's round(...,4) convention). test_desk_prompt_determinism asserts double-render byte equality. Sampling params pinned in config: temperature=0, fixed max_tokens, and a fully-qualified pinned model ID (exact dated model string, never an alias like 'latest' — a silent model upgrade is a strategy change and goes through the same gate as a prompt edit). TIER 2 — output determinism (best-effort, honestly bounded): temperature-0 LLM sampling is still not bit-reproducible across API calls, so the design does NOT pretend same-snapshot->same-verdict is cryptographically guaranteed; instead it makes every verdict REPLAYABLE and drift MEASURABLE: the full rendered request and full raw response for all five calls are stored as content-addressed blobs (sha256-named, under output/desk_blobs/), referenced from the journal row. scripts/replay_verdict.py takes a verdict_id, reconstructs the exact historical request from blobs, and either (a) re-parses the stored response through the current pipeline (pure, exact) or (b) re-invokes the pinned model and diffs the new verdict against the stored one — drift on the BINARY gates is the metric that matters and is reported per agent (thesis prose may vary; gates flipping at temperature 0 on identical input is an agent-prompt bug to escalate). Golden fixtures (test_desk_golden_verdicts) freeze recorded responses so the entire parse->aggregate->journal pipeline is regression-tested offline, deterministic, and API-free in CI. Version stamps (agent hash, model ID, strategy.yaml hash, engine git SHA) in every row mean any verdict is attributable to an exact (code, prompt, config, model) tuple — the audit-level determinism §10 actually needs.
latency_budget: Constraint: signals compute on closed candles, orders activate next bar (architecture invariant 3), and §5 entries are LIMIT orders at the retest — the limit must be working early in the bar after the trigger candle closes or the retest fill is fictional relative to the backtest's fill model. Base cadence is the 1m bar even for 5m triggers (a 5m trigger closes on a 1m boundary), so the budget is: TOTAL DESK BUDGET 30 s from snapshot receipt to Verdict handed to the Vault, HARD DEADLINE 45 s (fail-closed backstop), leaving >=15 s of the 60 s bar for Vault checks + order placement. Breakdown (all values live in config/strategy.yaml under a desk: block with § comments, CALIBRATE from measured Phase-5 latencies, never hard-coded): ingest+validate+filter+render <= 2 s (pure Python, realistically <100 ms); four specialist calls dispatched CONCURRENTLY (asyncio.gather), per-call timeout 20 s; single retry only if it fits inside the per-call window (first failure < 10 s in); aggregation + Hermes <= 8 s. Feasibility: each specialist call is one completion, ~2-4K prompt tokens (a filtered slice is small — the whole Snapshot is a few KB) and ~300-500 output tokens of JSON; on current pinned Claude models that is p50 ~4-8 s, p99 comfortably under 20 s; wall time of the parallel fan-out = slowest call, so p50 total ~ 8-12 s, p99 ~ 25-28 s — inside budget with margin. Hermes input is tiny (four small JSONs), ~3-5 s if it is an LLM call at all (see open questions: unanimity itself should be computed in deterministic Python; the LLM at most composes the thesis). FAIL-CLOSED ON BREACH: any specialist over 20 s => cancelled => FAIL => veto (veto_reason=timeout); total elapsed > 30 s at assembly => veto (veto_reason=latency_breach); the 45 s hard deadline force-closes the grading with a veto row even if calls are somehow still pending. LOGGING: every verdict row records per-agent dispatch_ts, completion_ts, latency_ms, retry_count, timed_out flag, plus total_latency_ms — on SUCCESSFUL gradings too, so the budget is recalibrated from measured p50/p99 during Phase-5 paper trading rather than asserted.
logging_journal: Extends the §10 strict-schema journal ('all verdicts — taken/skipped/vetoed — logged') to the Desk with one APPEND-ONLY row per grading, pydantic-validated (JournalRow, extra='forbid') before write; an invalid row halts the Desk (a verdict that can't be logged can't be proposed). Storage: JSONL (or SQLite append-only table) at output/desk_journal/, file opened append-mode only; full I/O lives in content-addressed blobs (output/desk_blobs/sha256.json) referenced from the row, keeping rows strict-schema and small while preserving the complete audit trail. Row schema: verdict_id (ULID, the join key the Vault reuses), graded_at_ts; trigger identity block (ts, tf, direction, kind, pattern, htf_flag, confluence_count — the exact Trigger fields); snapshot_ref (sha256 of the canonical Snapshot JSON blob); per-agent block for all five: {agent_name, agent_version, agent_sha256, model_id, request_blob_ref, response_blob_ref, parsed_verdict | error_code, latency_ms, retry_count, timed_out}; gates: the full union of every specialist's declared gates as {gate_name: pass|fail}, each gate name carrying its § reference (e.g. 'confluence_min_s7', 'rr_floor_s6_5'); hermes_verdict: the pinned Verdict JSON {trade, pattern, direction, entry, stop, target, size, grade, thesis, gates} exactly as delivered to the Vault (null if vetoed pre-assembly); outcome: proposed | vetoed | duplicate_suppressed; veto_reason enum (invalid_json, schema_violation, timeout, partial_completion, api_error, stale_snapshot, snapshot_trigger_ts_mismatch, engine_invariant_violation, invalid_snapshot, version_mismatch, latency_breach, runner_crash, gate_fail:<agent>); total_latency_ms; environment stamps: strategy_yaml_sha256, engine_git_sha, journal_schema_version. The Vault appends its OWN row (taken/skipped/vetoed-by-vault with reason) referencing verdict_id — the §10 requirement spans both layers via that join, and the nightly stats refresh / weekly Edge-Lab review (§10, PROPOSALS ONLY) reads the joined view. Crash-safety: write-ahead intent rows (see failure modes) guarantee no grading is ever absent from the journal. Enforcement in tests: test_desk_journal_schema_strict + a static check that the journal writer module exposes append only (no update/delete code paths).
versioning: Principle (ai-workflow-rules, verbatim intent): 'Prompt changes to agent files are versioned like code — a prompt edit IS a strategy change.' Mechanism: (1) every agent file's frontmatter carries version: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; (2) a committed lockfile .claude/agents/agents.lock maps each agent file to its sha256 content hash + version; (3) the Desk runner at startup hashes every agent file and refuses to run on any mismatch with the lockfile (fail-closed — an edited-but-unbumped prompt structurally cannot grade a live candidate); (4) every journal row stamps all five agents' (version, sha256) plus model_id, strategy.yaml sha256, and engine git SHA, so any historical verdict is attributable to the exact (prompt, config, code, model) tuple and any behavioral change across time is diffable to a specific version transition. Because the Snapshot-field allowlist and the verbatim strategy-doc slice live INSIDE the agent file, changing what an agent sees or which rules it holds changes the hash — there is no unversionable edit surface. Change process rides the existing gate: written hypothesis -> Angus approval -> version bump + lockfile update + progress-tracker.md entry in the SAME commit (a CI consistency check fails if agent-file hashes and agents.lock diverge, making the paired update mandatory); model-ID changes and sampling-param changes go through the identical gate because they are recorded in the same lockfile. Strategy-doc coupling: each agent file names the constitution version it slices (strategy-definition-v1.0.md); test_desk_verbatim_slice string-matches every embedded slice against the actual doc, so a future doc bump to v1.1 breaks CI until every affected agent file is re-verified and re-versioned — agent prompts can never silently lag the constitution.
testing_plan: test_desk_allowlist_filter — render each specialist's REAL prompt from a fully-populated synthetic Snapshot+Trigger; assert every out-of-lane field name AND value is absent from the rendered request string; the filtered dict contains exactly the declared paths.

test_desk_allowlist_paths_valid — every dot-path declared in every agent file resolves against Snapshot.model_json_schema()/Trigger.model_json_schema(); an unknown path aborts Desk startup (guards against Snapshot field renames silently emptying a slice).

test_desk_fail_closed_invalid_json — mocked specialist returns (a) non-JSON prose, (b) truncated JSON, (c) valid JSON missing a gate, (d) valid JSON with an extra field, (e) wrong enum value; each case => specialist FAIL => veto, correct veto_reason, raw blob preserved.

test_desk_unanimity_veto — parametrized over each single specialist failing (gate fail OR error) while three pass => Verdict.trade=false, vetoed; all four pass => proposed; two failing => veto lists both.
test_desk_timeout_veto — mocked slow specialist beyond per-call timeout => cancelled, FAIL, latency_ms logged, veto; other three verdicts still journaled.
test_desk_partial_completion — one specialist never returns; total deadline expiry => veto with partial_completion naming the missing agent.

test_desk_specialist_independence_static — static scan of every agent markdown: no occurrence of any other agent's name, output-schema keys, or verdict fields (Hermes exempted for verdict keys only); PLUS a signature-level check that the specialist dispatch function accepts no verdict-typed parameter — cross-referencing is impossible, not just discouraged.

test_desk_no_outbound_import — mirror of the Vault's no-LLM-import test (architecture invariant 6), inverted: walk the import graph of src/desk/*; forbid telegram, broker/order modules, src/vault, and any network client other than the pinned Anthropic SDK — the Desk proposes and cannot act.
test_vault_no_desk_llm_import — re-assert the existing invariant from the Vault side once src/desk exists: no import path from Vault to any LLM-calling module.

test_desk_golden_verdicts — golden fixtures: N recorded (snapshot, trigger, five raw model responses) tuples replayed offline through the full parse->aggregate->journal pipeline => byte-identical Verdict JSON and journal rows; zero API calls in CI; fixtures include at least one pass, one gate-fail veto, one malformed-response veto per specialist.

test_desk_duplicate_trigger_suppressed — identical trigger dispatched twice => one grading, second writes duplicate_suppressed referencing the original verdict_id; dedupe set survives a simulated restart (rebuilt from journal).
test_desk_stale_snapshot_veto — (a) Snapshot.ts != Trigger.ts => veto snapshot_trigger_ts_mismatch; (b) dispatch wall-clock beyond desk.staleness_limit_s => veto stale_snapshot with drift_ms logged.

test_desk_conflicting_triggers_veto — two triggers sharing a close ts injected post-arbitration => both vetoed engine_invariant_violation (and the arbitration property itself is already covered in test_triggers.py: at most one Trigger per ts).
test_desk_version_lock — tamper one byte of an agent file without updating agents.lock => runner refuses to start; every journal row carries all five (version, sha256) stamps.
test_desk_lockfile_ci_consistency — CI check: hash every .claude/agents/*.md and compare to agents.lock; any drift fails the build (forces version bump + progress-tracker entry in the same commit).
test_desk_verbatim_slice — each agent file's embedded strategy-doc slice string-matches the current strategy-definition-v1.0.md verbatim; breaks on any doc version bump until slices are re-verified.
test_desk_journal_schema_strict — every row validates against JournalRow (extra='forbid'); an invalid row halts the Desk; writer module is append-only (no update/delete paths).
test_desk_crash_recovery — intent row without a verdict row at startup => synthetic veto row runner_crash appended.
test_desk_latency_logged — per-agent latency_ms, retry_count, timed_out and total_latency_ms present on BOTH successful and vetoed gradings.
test_desk_prompt_determinism — rendering the same (snapshot, trigger, agent version) twice yields byte-identical request payloads (no timestamps, uuids, or env state in prompts).
test_desk_hermes_input_isolation — Hermes's rendered input contains only the four specialist verdict JSONs + trigger identity keys; no raw Snapshot market fields (orchestration only).
backtest_vs_live: THE IMPLICATION, stated plainly: architecture.md pins backtest mode as Desk-bypassed — triggers.py IS the ruleset, and every validated expectancy number (calibration vs the 28 hand trades, tournaments, Monte Carlo pass-probability in §12.6) describes a system WITHOUT the Desk. Live adds a veto-only layer: the Desk can remove trades from the validated distribution but never add one. So graded-live is guaranteed to trade a SUBSET of the backtest's trades, and the backtest's expectancy transfers to live only under the assumption 'Desk approves everything triggers.py approves'. Every veto is a divergence from the validated distribution in an unknown direction — vetoing would-be losers silently improves live vs backtest, vetoing would-be winners silently degrades it, and either way the Monte Carlo eval-pass math (§12.6) computed on the unvetoed distribution no longer describes the live system. This must be MEASURED, not vibed. PHASE-5 MEASUREMENT DESIGN (the shadow ledger): during paper trading (§12.7 — agents grade real-time, human executes), run the backtester's deterministic resolution engine in SHADOW on the same live bars: for EVERY trigger the engine emits, record a joined row {verdict_id, desk_outcome (proposed/vetoed + veto_reason + failing gate + failing agent), shadow_outcome_R (what the backtest ruleset says this trade would have made, resolved on the actual subsequent bars with the same fill/slippage model)}. Both legs consume the identical Market Engine, so the candidate sets match by construction and the delta is purely the Desk. Metrics reported in the §10 weekly review (PROPOSALS ONLY, Angus sign-off for any change): (1) veto rate, overall and split by gate CLASS — mechanical re-derivation gates (confluence count §7, RR floor §6.5, window §1, location §7...) vs judgment-shaped gates — with the standing expectation that MECHANICAL-gate vetoes should be ~0 because triggers.py already enforced them; any nonzero mechanical veto is either an engine bug or stale config and is escalated IMMEDIATELY as a defect, which is precisely the cross-check value the Desk exists for; (2) expectancy-of-vetoed vs expectancy-of-approved in shadow R: did vetoes add or destroy R, with bootstrap CIs given small N; (3) operational veto rate (timeout/api_error/invalid_json vetoes) tracked SEPARATELY from substantive vetoes — an operational veto of a shadow winner is an infrastructure cost, not a judgment signal, and its rate bounds how much backtest expectancy the runtime itself is burning; (4) live-approved distribution vs shadow-all distribution comparison feeding a REVISED Monte Carlo before any funded evaluation (§12.6 rerun on the veto-adjusted distribution). Acceptance framing for Angus at end of Phase 5: 'the Desk vetoed X% of triggers, costing/saving Y R vs backtest expectation, with mechanical-gate agreement at Z%' — a measured delta, with the anti-tuning guardrail intact: divergences are reported, never patched by loosening agent prompts to match the backtest.
open_questions_for_spec3: Is unanimity aggregation pure Python in the runner (recommended: unanimity is arithmetic and must be fail-closed-deterministic; the Hermes LLM call would then ONLY compose the human-readable thesis), or does the Hermes LLM own aggregation? The architecture diagram says 'Hermes polls -> specialists, unanimity or no' — spec 3 must pin which half of Hermes is code and which is prompt.

If all four specialists pass but Hermes thesis composition fails/times out, is the trade vetoed (strict fail-closed reading, my default) or proposed with a machine-generated stub thesis? This trades a valid §-compliant setup against prose generation — trading-semantics-adjacent, so per the escalation rule: Angus.

Concrete numeric sign-off for the desk: config block — per-call timeout 20 s, total budget 30 s, hard deadline 45 s, staleness_limit_s 10 — proposed here as CALIBRATE start values; where do they live (strategy.yaml desk: block with § comments per architecture invariant 5, or a separate desk.yaml) and do they recalibrate from Phase-5 measured p50/p99 through the normal gate?

Pinned model ID and cost ceiling: 4-5 calls per trigger x expected triggers/day — which exact dated Claude model is pinned for Phase 3, and is there a per-day API spend guard (an operational limit, arguably a Vault-adjacent concern that must not live in the Desk)?

Entry-window ownership: does the engine pre-filter triggers outside the active W-variant window (§1) so the Desk never sees them, or does the Desk grade everything and Helios re-derives the window gate? Recommendation: engine pre-filters (the Desk graded set should equal the backtest candidate set for the shadow ledger to join cleanly), with Helios still re-deriving as cross-check — needs pinning.

Idempotency key definition: proposed sha256(Trigger.ts, tf, direction, kind) + snapshot hash — confirm this uniquely identifies a candidate under all engine behaviors (e.g. can a re-run emit the same ts/tf with a different entry_ref after a config recalibration mid-Phase-5?).

Verdict schema semantics: the pinned schema has both 'size' and 'grade' — spec 3 must define grade's domain (full/half unit conviction per §9? a letter grade?) and the exact boundary between Hephaestus proposing size class (full/half per §9) and the Vault owning absolute contract count (MC-derived ceiling, §9/§10).

Should Snapshot (or the dispatch envelope) carry the active strategy.yaml content hash and entry-window variant so specialists re-derive gates against the SAME config the engine used, rather than the runner reading strategy.yaml at render time (a race if config changes intra-session)? This also makes stale-config detection — a core Desk value — explicit: the agent file states thresholds symbolically (cluster.tolerance_points) and the envelope supplies the values with their hash.

Blob and journal retention/rotation policy for the Phase-4 VPS (full request/response blobs accumulate; disk is finite on a 'small always-on VPS' per architecture.md) — retention is an audit-integrity decision, not just ops.

Retry policy strictness: is the single within-budget retry on API error acceptable, or does the strictest fail-closed reading demand zero retries (any API error = immediate veto)? Cost: a transient 429 veto burns a potentially valid setup; benefit: simpler determinism story. Needs an explicit decision recorded in spec 3.

Does the Desk runner run in the same process as the live engine loop or as a separate service with a queue? Affects crash-recovery semantics (write-ahead intent rows) and whether a Desk halt (journal write failure, version mismatch) also halts trigger detection or only grading.
